findings.summary: An authorized Repair cannot reach the next independent-review dispatch state.
findings.evidence: review-decision.ts records review-decision.json for --repair but leaves the existing independent-review.json in place (lines 87-119). task-status.ts defines review_ready only when !reviewExists (lines 142-150), and after a stale review routes to fix-independent-review-record (lines 177-181). independent-review.ts --prepare only rewrites review-packet.md (lines 74-86). After the Builder changes governed files, the old review is stale; even with fresh Evidence and a fresh packet, the existing review file keeps review_ready false, so the documented Repair -> fresh review cycle has no legal dispatch state. No test covers this transition.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit review-round reset/rotation, or make a stale review record count as absent for review_ready after a fresh packet. Add an end-to-end regression covering valid review -> explicit selected Repair -> governed change -> fresh Evidence/packet -> review_ready true -> new review verification.

findings.summary: The claimed Token-efficiency target is not reproduced or bound by the task Evidence.
findings.evidence: classification.yaml states that the three-times-baseline Token target requires a fresh paired replay and cannot be proven by repository unit tests; change-impact-analysis.md lists that replay in the verification scope. test-plan.md records historical measurements of 7,545,974 versus 3,220,846 tokens (2.34x), while evidence.json contains only check/typecheck/test PASS records and no replay artifact or provenance. Thus the repository gates establish lifecycle correctness but do not establish the performance goal named by the task.
findings.recommendation: Run and attach a fresh paired replay with reproducible inputs, session classification, and Token accounting, or explicitly narrow the task acceptance claim to the lifecycle/adapter behavior covered by the repository tests.
